meta.title: CamCon | Film-look photos on your phone, the instant you shoot
meta.desc: CamCon links your DSLR or mirrorless camera to Android over USB or Wi-Fi and delivers film-simulated photos to your phone the moment you press the shutter. A cinema camera controller.
a11y.showcaseAlt: Photo with a CamCon film simulation applied
hero.title: Press the shutter, and the film-look photo lands on your phone
hero.sub: Connect your camera over USB or Wi-Fi and receive photos with a film simulation already applied, right as you shoot.
features.title: From capture to color, bridged between camera and phone
feat.wifi.d: Receive photos instantly over PTP/IP, no cable needed. It reconnects automatically if the link drops and keeps receiving in the background.
feat.usb.d: A rock-solid wired connection built on standard PTP. Plug in a USB-C (OTG) cable and your camera is recognized instantly.
feat.film.d: 3D LUTs modeled on real film stocks, applied automatically to every shot. You receive the photo with the film look already baked in.
feat.color.d: Pull the color from a single reference photo you love and apply it to your own shots.
feat.live.d: Watch a real-time preview while adjusting ISO, shutter, aperture and white balance. Choose from three quality levels: speed, balance, quality.
feat.timelapse.d: Unattended interval shooting is in the works. For now, shots are taken one at a time with the remote shutter.
feat.raw.d: Download RAW originals (NEF and more) losslessly. The film look is applied only to a JPG copy, so your original stays untouched.
feat.auto.d: Just power on your camera: CamCon discovers and reconnects it automatically via mDNS/SSDP. No setup every time.
films.title: 9 families, 296 film simulations
films.lead: From black & white to instant and color negative: real film tone curves and color, reproduced as 3D LUTs.
films.freeLabel: Free Signature: 5 signature films, free to use
films.note: The look is baked in by the receiving pipeline the instant you shoot, and your RAW originals are never touched. PRO opens the full catalog and film + color applied together.
films.baHint: Tap a film to switch, and drag the handle to compare before and after.
color.title: One photo becomes your preset
color.lead: CamCon reads the color distribution out of a photo you like and moves it onto yours. Even a look that isn't in the catalog carries over from a single reference.
color.refAlt: Reference photo the color is taken from
color.targetAlt: Original photo before the color is applied
color.resultAlt: Result photo with the reference color applied
color.dragHint: Drag the handle to compare before and after.
color.note: At 0% you get the original untouched; at 100% the color distribution matches the reference exactly. Like film, it is applied only to the JPG copy, so your RAW originals are never touched. PRO lets you run film and color together.
cameras.title: Will my camera work?
cameras.lead: If your camera supports USB (PTP) or Wi-Fi STA (router) mode, it works with CamCon.
cameras.usbDesc: PTP-compatible cameras connected with a USB-C (OTG) cable. Supports major makers: Nikon, Canon, Sony, Fujifilm, Panasonic, OM System (Olympus), Pentax, Ricoh, Leica and more.
cameras.wifiDesc: Wireless (Wi-Fi) connection currently supports the Nikon Z series (Z6 and Z8 verified on real hardware). Canon, Sony and Fujifilm wireless is under verification. Support is expanding. Other makers can connect right away over USB.
cameras.unified: Whether you connect over USB or Wi-Fi, every feature (capture, transfer, film looks) is identical.
cameras.listNote: The list below shows PTP (USB) compatible models. Models with the Wi-Fi badge support wireless connection.
cameras.searchPh: Search by brand or model (e.g. Nikon Z8)

cameras.help: Most cameras that support a PTP/MTP USB connection will work. If you're unsure, contact us and we'll check for you.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: How do I check whether my camera is supported?
faq.a1: If your camera supports USB (PTP) or Wi-Fi STA (router) mode, it works with CamCon. There's no difference in features depending on how you connect. You can search for your model under "Browse all supported models" above.
faq.q2: Will my RAW files be altered?
faq.a2: RAW originals are preserved as-is. The film simulation and color are applied only to a JPG copy; RAW files (NEF and more) are never modified.
faq.q3: Does it keep receiving in the background?
faq.a3: It runs as a foreground service, so it keeps receiving while you use other apps. Receiving stops only if you fully close the app.
faq.q4: Which Android version do I need?
faq.a4: Android 10 or later on a 64-bit (arm64) device.
faq.q5: Where do I enter a referral code?
faq.a5: You can enter it on the login screen, or under Settings → Register referral code.
faq.a6: On the Nikon Z series, you must approve "Allow connection" on the camera body the first time you connect. Turn on your phone's hotspot, or make sure the camera and phone are on the same Wi-Fi router. If it still fails, turn the camera's Wi-Fi off and on again, then search again in the app.
faq.q7: What can I do for free?
faq.a7: Camera connection (USB and Wi-Fi), shooting, photo transfer and 5 signature films are free. On the free plan, photos are saved at up to 2000px on the long edge. PRO unlocks all 296 film simulations, full-resolution saving, RAW downloads and advanced live view control.
faq.q8: Are photos taken with the camera's shutter button transferred too?
faq.a8: Yes. On supported cameras, photos taken with the camera body's shutter (not just remote shots from the app) are transferred to your phone automatically. This also works while live view is on.
faq.a9: CamCon is currently Android-only (Android 10 or later, 64-bit arm64 devices). There is no iOS version.

guide.meta.title: How to Connect a Nikon Camera over Wi-Fi | CamCon
guide.meta.desc: Connect a Nikon Z camera to CamCon wirelessly in five steps, using only your phone hotspot. No router needed. Includes what to check when the connection fails.
guide.h1: Connecting a Nikon Camera over Wi-Fi
guide.lead: No router required. The camera joins your phone hotspot directly, so it works outdoors just as well. Set it up once and afterwards the camera connects as soon as you switch it on.
guide.toc.title: On this page
guide.prep.title: What you need
guide.prep.body: An Android phone that can share a hotspot, a Nikon Z series camera, and the CamCon app. No cable and no router.
guide.prep.note.title: If your camera is not a Nikon
guide.prep.note.body: Wireless connection is currently verified for the Nikon Z series. Please connect Canon, Sony, Fujifilm and other brands with a USB cable. Wired connection works with far more models.
guide.steps.title: Connecting
guide.steps.body: Five steps. Most people get stuck on the third and the fifth, so pay attention to those two.
guide.s1.title: Turn on the hotspot on your phone
guide.s1.body: The camera joins your phone directly, so nothing passes through a router. In CamCon, the Wi-Fi connection screen has a button that opens the hotspot settings for you.
guide.s1.tip: Turning on the hotspot usually switches your phone Wi-Fi off automatically. That is expected, so just leave it.
guide.s1.cap: You will type this name and password into the camera in the next step.
guide.s2.title: Join that hotspot from the camera
guide.s2.body: Open the network settings in the camera menu, pick the hotspot you just turned on and enter the password. Menu names differ slightly between models.
guide.s2.path: MENU ▸ Network ▸ Connect to computer ▸ Network settings
guide.s2.cap: You can look up the exact menu location for your model in the official Nikon manual.
guide.s3.title: Set the connection type to camera control
guide.s3.body: The same network menu contains an option for the connection type. Be sure to choose camera control.
guide.s3.note.title: With image transfer it connects, but only halfway
guide.s3.note.body: Photos taken during live view will not arrive right away, and you cannot browse the memory card. CamCon detects this state and tells you, but the setting has to be changed on the camera.
guide.s3.cap: Choose the upper one to get shooting, live view and card browsing all at once.
guide.s4.title: Search for the camera in CamCon
guide.s4.body: Open the Wi-Fi connection screen in the app, select the phone hotspot tab and tap search. If the camera has joined the hotspot, the model name appears within a few seconds.
guide.s4.cap: The model name and maker are identified before connecting. Check that it is your own camera before selecting it.
guide.s5.title: Allow the connection on the camera
guide.s5.body: Selecting the camera from the list does not connect it right away. A prompt appears on the camera asking whether to allow the connection, and you have to confirm it on the camera itself.
guide.s5.note.title: If the app looks frozen, look at the camera
guide.s5.note.body: At this point the app is waiting for the camera to answer. Nothing moves on screen so it feels like a failure, but in most cases the camera is simply waiting for your permission.
guide.s5.shot.body:
Connect to the smart device?
Press OK to connect.
guide.s5.cap: Once allowed, later connections happen automatically without this step.
guide.done.title: Once connected
guide.done.body: Photos land on your phone the moment you press the shutter. If a film simulation is on, they arrive with the look already applied. Live view and shooting settings can be controlled from the phone as well.
guide.models.title: Models verified over Wi-Fi
guide.models.body: These models have been connected and verified on real hardware.
guide.models.note: Nikon models not on this list may well work too. They are simply not listed because we have not verified them on real hardware yet.
guide.trouble.title: If it does not connect
guide.trouble.body: Work down the list in order. The first three solve most cases.
guide.t1.title: Is a permission prompt waiting on the camera?
guide.t1.body: This is by far the most common cause. While the app waits, check the camera screen and press the confirm button.
guide.t2.title: Is the connection type set to image transfer?
guide.t2.body: If it connects but photos never arrive or the card is invisible, this setting is the reason. Go back to step three.
guide.t3.title: Has the camera actually joined the hotspot?
guide.t3.body: Check that your phone hotspot is the selected entry in the camera Wi-Fi list. A single wrong character in the password prevents the connection.
guide.t4.title: Has power saving switched the camera radio off?
guide.t4.body: Nikon cameras turn the radio off after a period without input. Half press the shutter button to wake it, then search again.
guide.t5.title: Is the phone hotspot still on?
guide.t5.body: Battery savers sometimes switch the hotspot off on their own. Also check the option that turns it off after a while when no device is connected.
guide.t6.title: Still nothing? Turn the camera off and on again
guide.t6.body: A previous session can linger on the camera and block a new one. Power cycling clears it.
guide.end.title: You can also connect with a cable
guide.end.body: All you need is a USB cable, and it works with far more models than Wi-Fi. If your camera is not a Nikon, use this route.
guide.router: Indoors with a router available, joining the camera and phone to the same router works exactly the same way. In that case skip the first step and start from the second.
ghub.meta.title: How to Connect Your Camera | CamCon
ghub.meta.desc: Step by step wireless connection guides for Nikon, Canon, Sony and Fujifilm cameras, one per brand. Cable connection is covered too.
ghub.lead: Menu names and settings differ from brand to brand. Pick your camera maker and you will get the steps that match it.
ghub.pick.title: Choose your camera maker
ghub.nikon.desc: Join the hotspot, then set the connection type to camera control.
ghub.canon.desc: Pick the EOS Utility connection under network functions.
ghub.sony.desc: Turn PC remote on and access authentication off.
ghub.fuji.desc: Save a network setting, then switch the connection mode.
ghub.usb.title: If you would rather use a cable
ghub.usb.body: Connecting by USB works the same way for every brand and covers far more models than Wi-Fi. Plug the cable in, allow the permission in the app, and you are done.
g.status.untested.title: This brand has not been verified on real hardware yet
g.status.untested.body: The connection path is in place, so following the steps below has a good chance of working. We simply have not been able to test it on a camera of this brand ourselves. Telling us either way helps a lot.
gn.gen.new.title: Newer bodies such as Z9, Z8, Z6III, Zf and Z5
gn.gen.old.title: Earlier bodies such as Z7II, Z6II, Z7 and Z6
gn.gen.note: Only the menu location differs; what you do inside is the same. Either way, create a network setting and leave the connection type on camera control.
gc.meta.title: How to Connect a Canon Camera over Wi-Fi | CamCon
gc.meta.desc: How to join a Canon EOS camera to your phone hotspot, set it to the EOS Utility connection and shoot remotely from CamCon.
gc.h1: Connecting a Canon Camera over Wi-Fi
gc.lead: Canon calls remote computer control the EOS Utility connection. Pick that one item correctly and the rest is straightforward.
gc.s2.body: Under network functions, add a device and create a new setting, then pick your phone hotspot from the list and enter the password.
gc.s2.path: MENU ▸ Network settings ▸ Connect to EOS Utility
gc.s3.title: Leave the address on automatic and turn IPv6 off
gc.s3.body: When the address screen appears, leave IPv4 on automatic and set IPv6 to disabled. Then simply confirm the values shown and continue.
gc.s3.note.title: Choosing the smartphone connection blocks remote shooting
gc.s3.note.body: The same network menu also offers a smartphone connection and FTP transfer. Those open the camera for file transfer only, so shooting control will not work.
gc.s5.body: Once the setup is done, the camera screen switches to waiting for pairing. Select the camera in the app at that point and the connection completes.
gc.t1.title: Is the connection set to EOS Utility?
gc.t1.body: If it is set to smartphone connection or FTP, the camera shows up but shooting control will not work. Check the setting again under network functions.
gc.t2.title: Is IPv6 still enabled?
gc.t2.body: With IPv6 on, the camera sometimes fails to get a usable address and never shows up in the search. Set it to disabled and try again.
gs.meta.title: How to Connect a Sony Camera over Wi-Fi | CamCon
gs.meta.desc: How to join a Sony Alpha camera to your phone hotspot, turn PC remote on and shoot from CamCon. Includes why access authentication has to be off.
gs.h1: Connecting a Sony Camera over Wi-Fi
gs.lead: Sony spreads the settings across three places: joining Wi-Fi, turning PC remote on, and turning access authentication off. Miss any one of them and the connection fails.
gs.s2.body: In the network menu, switch Wi-Fi connect on, open the access point settings, pick your phone hotspot and enter the password.
gs.s2.path: MENU ▸ Network ▸ Wi-Fi ▸ Wi-Fi Connect ▸ Access Point Set.
gs.s3.title: Turn PC remote on and access authentication off
gs.s3.body: Under PC remote function in the network menu, switch PC remote on. Then, in network options, turn access authentication off. The two items live on different screens.
gs.s3.note.title: With access authentication on, the connection is refused
gs.s3.note.body: This is an authentication scheme added in recent Sony firmware. While it is on, any program connecting the standard way is blocked. If you would rather not leave the camera open, switch it back on after the shoot.
gs.s5.body: Sony often does not ask you to approve anything on the body. Select the camera in the app and it connects straight away, with a remote indicator appearing on the camera screen.
gs.t1.title: Is PC remote switched off?
gs.t1.body: If you only joined Wi-Fi without turning PC remote on, the camera will not accept control requests. Check PC remote function again in the network menu.
gs.t2.title: Is access authentication still on?
gs.t2.body: If the camera shows up in the search but every connection attempt fails, this setting is usually the reason. Turn it off in network options.
gf.meta.title: How to Connect a Fujifilm Camera over Wi-Fi | CamCon
gf.meta.desc: How to join a Fujifilm X or GFX camera to your phone hotspot, switch the connection mode and shoot remotely from CamCon.
gf.h1: Connecting a Fujifilm Camera over Wi-Fi
gf.lead: Fujifilm has you create and save a network setting. Skip the saving step and you will start over every time the camera is switched off.
gf.s2.body: In network settings, choose a network setting slot and switch the access point setting to manual. Pick your phone hotspot from the list, enter the password and save the setting.
gf.s3.title: Switch the connection mode to tethered shooting
gf.s3.body: The same network and USB settings menu holds a connection mode item. Choose the wireless tethered shooting mode. Leaving it on smartphone transfer means no shooting control.
gf.s3.note.title: If the IP address shows only asterisks, the join failed
gf.s3.note.body: It means the camera never received an address from the hotspot. Re-check the password, make sure the network setting was saved, and join again.
gf.s5.body: Select the camera in the app and it connects. Fujifilm uses its own communication scheme rather than the shared one, so it also appears a little differently in the search results.
gf.t1.title: Is the connection mode set to tethered shooting?
gf.t1.body: In smartphone transfer mode the camera only hands over photos and accepts no shooting control. Check the connection mode again under network and USB settings.
gf.t2.title: Did you save the network setting?
gf.t2.body: If you entered the password but never confirmed the save, the setting is not kept. If the connection disappeared after a power cycle, this is the likely cause.
g.s5.title: Select the camera in the app to finish
gn.wiz.title: Create a network profile with the connection wizard
gn.wiz.body: Choose create profile under network settings and the wizard asks five things in order. Answer them as shown below.
gn.wiz.v1: Leaving it as WLAN1 is fine
gn.wiz.v3: Your phone hotspot name in the list
gn.wiz.m1.cap: A phone hotspot has no pairing button, so you need the search option on top.
gn.wiz.m2.bar: How the IP address is obtained
gn.wiz.m2.cap: Entering it manually often leaves the address mismatched so the camera never shows up. Leave it automatic.
gn.pair.screen:
Pairing smart device and camera.
Start SnapBridge or NX MobileAir
on the smart device
and select the camera.
gn.pair.cap: Once this screen appears, the camera side is done.
gn.pair.note.title: You do not need SnapBridge
gn.pair.note.body: The camera names two Nikon apps, but you can use CamCon at that point instead. It is simply waiting in the standard way and does not care which app connects. A lot of people stop at this screen.
gn.t.band.title: Is the hotspot set to 5GHz?
gn.t.band.body: Some Nikon bodies only work on 2.4GHz and will not even list a 5GHz hotspot. Switch the band to 2.4GHz in your phone hotspot settings and search again.
gn.tip.auto.title: If the card is full of photos, turn auto transfer off first
gn.tip.auto.body: If auto transfer in the same menu is on, everything already on the card starts coming over the moment you connect. Turn it off before connecting and back on afterwards, and only the photos you take from then on arrive.
gn.tip.code.title: Some bodies show an authentication code
gn.tip.code.body: If a few digits appear on the camera screen, type them into the app. More bodies do not show one at all, so its absence is not a problem.
gn.t.recon.title: Did it drop once right after the first pairing?
gn.t.recon.body: On some bodies the connection drops once as pairing completes. That is not a fault, it means the registration finished. Connect once more from the app and it stays up from then on.
gn.shot.menu: In the network menu, open connect to computer and choose network settings.
gn.shot.name: It asks for a profile name. Leaving it as WLAN1 is fine.
